LD 93 -- An Act to Reduce Cost and Increase Access to Disease Prevention by Expanding the
Universal Childhood Immunization Program to Include Adults
Senator ingwersen, Representative Meyer, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services:
My name is Caitlin Gilmet, and i serve as the Director of Maine Families for Vaccines, a coalition of
parents, healthcare advocates, and public health professionals committed to ensuring access to life-saving immunizations for all Mainers. I appreciate the opportunity to provide testimony on LD 93, which seeks to expand Maine's Universal Childhood Immunization Program to include adults.
Maine's existing Universal Childhood immunization Program has been a national modelfor ensuring broad vaccine access while lowering costs for families, providers, and insurers. This
program has supported high childhood vaccination rates, with 95% of school-age children receiving
required immunizations as of August 2024. LD 93 presents an opportunity to build on this strong foundation and extend similar benefits to adult populations, where coverage gaps remain a
challenge.
As we consider this expansion, it's important to acknowledge that the federal landscape for vaccine
programs is changing. With potential shifts in vaccine funding, supply chains, and policy frameworks, states must be proactive in ensuring that immunization programs remain strong, sustainable, and adaptable to future challenges.
Providers are the most trusted voices in vaccine education, and their role in immunization efforts is critical. Any system expansion must ensure that healthcare providers are adequately supported, empowered, and fairly reimbursed for both vaccine administration and patient counseling. The ability to provide clear, evidence-based guidance to patients is essential for maintaining high immunization rates and public trust in vaccines.
Additionally, broad access and choice must be preserved within the program. A strong universal purchase model should maintain a full range of ACIP-recommended vaccines without limiting choice. Vaccine access is not just about supply; it's about ensuring that patients and providers have options that meet medical, logistical, and personal needs. Other states with Universal Purchase programs have faced challenges when access to certain formulations was restricted, which can contribute to vaccine hesitancy and make it more challenging for small practices to provide immunizations in a medical home.

Maine Families for Vaccines supports expanding vaccine access, strengthening vaccine policy, and ensuring equity in immunization programs. This bill presents an opportunity to bolster our state's immunization infrastructure and better protect Mainers of all ages.
We encourage this committee to advance LD 93 with a focus on preserving access, empowering
providers, and ensuring the program remains responsive to the needs of Maine communities. Thank you for your time and consideration.

Written Testimony of the Maine Chapter of the American College of Physicians
In Support of
LD 93 An Act to Reduce Cost and Increase Access to Disease Prevention by Expanding the Universal Childhood Immunization Program to Include Adults
Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services Room 209, Cross Building, Augusta, Maine Wednesday, February 5, 2025
Good afternoon, Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer, and Members of the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services,
My name is Stephen Hayes, MD and I am the current governor of the Maine Chapter of the American College of Physicians. I am submitting this written testimony in support of LD 93, An Act to Reduce Cost and Increase Access to Disease Prevention by Expanding the Universal Childhood Immunization Program to Include Adults. I am providing this testimony on the behalf of the Maine Chapter of the American College of Physicians.
The Maine Chapter of the American College of Physicians is a group of internal medicine specialists representing more than 500 practicing physicians, resident physicians and medical students in the state of Maine. As internal medicine specialists, we provide care to adults in both the inpatient and outpatient settings. The American College of physicians represents more than 100,000 internal medicine specialists, residents and medical students across United States and abroad.

The Maine Chapter of the American College of Physicians recognizes the vital importance of immunizations in promoting the health and wellbeing of all Mainers. We recognize the vital role the childhood immunization program has played in providing access to vaccines to all eligible citizens. Many adults in our state experience barriers to accessing vaccines. Many lack health insurance coverage and many have high deductible insurance plans that make all elements of care difficult to afford. By expanding the immunization program to include vaccine coverage for adults between ages 19 and 64, we will have the opportunity to make these important treatments accessible to a greater number of people.
Our national organization recognizes the importance of vaccine therapy. It is a stated policy of our national organization to support state laws that are designed to promote access to all recommended immunizations
On behalf of the Maine Chapter the American College of Physicians, I would like to reiterate our support for this important bill. We believe that this provides an opportunity to improve the health of our fellow citizens and has the potential help reduce overall costs to the health care system.
Thank you for allowing me to provide input from the Maine Chapter of the American College of Physicians on this important pill and we hope you will support LD 93.
Thank you,
Stephen R. Hayes, MD, MACP
Governor, Maine Chapter of the American College of Physicians.

Testimony regarding LD 93 2/5/2025
Sydney R. Sewall, MD MPH (Hallowell)
Sen. Ingwersen, Rep. Meyer, and members of the HHS committee--

As many of you know, I have been a pediatrician in this area since 1982. In
2011-2012, I participated in the meetings that created the current universal
immunization program in our state -- which pays the vaccine costs for ALL
children through age 18. Months of discussions involving insurers, vaccine manufacturers, Mainecare, the Maine Immunization Program, and physicians (especially Maine AAP) led to the establishment of an efficient and smoothrunning system that expanded access and lowered health care costs in the state.
Remarkably, all the original players are still pleased with the outcome.
How does the system work? The CDC gets a substantial discount for its bulk
purchasing of vaccines. The Maine Immunization Program pools funds from the Federal Vaccines for Children (VFC) program, Mainecare, and private insurers --- and uses these funds to buy products at these reduced prices. Insurers are happy since they pay less to provide a necessary preventive service Vaccine manufacturers are happy, since the increased volume compensates for
the decrease in unit price.

Pediatricians and PP physicians are enormously satisfied with the change.
P111013 to this law in my own practice, we needed to have separate storage for
vaccines used for Mainecare kids vs. private pay patients. At one point we
maintained 5 refrigerators and freezers in our office in Augusta to store and track the vaccines used for these different populations, even though the
products were identical.

Billing was also complicated, and some families got hit with unexpected expenses -- or our office had to absorb the product cost without compensation.
This scenario will be eliminated for adult practitioners with passage of LD 93 -
making Maine a more attractive site for young physicians to set up practice.

pricing web site:

My name is Trevor Putnoky and I'm the President and CEO of the Healthcare Purchaser Alliance of Maine.
The HPA is a nonprofit that represents the purchasers of health care in Maine. Our mission is to advance
and support access to high-quality, affordable care. We have over 60 members, including some of the
largest public and private employers and health trusts in Maine. Collectively, our members spend over a

billion dollars annually providing health care for nearly one quarter of the commercially insured population

in the state.

V

|'m here today to testify in support of LD 93. The Maine Vaccine Board's childhood vaccine program currently saves public and commercial payers in Maine millions of dollars by purchasing vaccines in bulk at
discounted federal contract rates that are passed through to those payers. We understand from the bill
sponsor that extending the program to include adult vaccines would allow commercially insured health plans to leverage that bulk purchasing power to procure vaccines for adults at lower prices as well. In fact, other states that have implemented similar legislation have typically seen savings of 20 percent for adult vaccines?

Maine employers and employees are struggling to afford the cost of providing healthcare coverage to their employees and families, with premiums continuing to increase at a significantly higher rate than wages and inflation. Medication costs are a significant-and growing--part of those high premiums. As employers
work to keep the cost of healthcare coverage affordable for their organizations and their employees, we
are grateful for Rep. Zager to put forward a proposal that is designed to lower the cost of essential and
cost-effective vaccines.
